name: Claude Code /design Command — Research Preview; In-Terminal UI Artboards; Anthropic Official
hook: Shipped August 17 by Nate Parrott (Anthropic design team): a new /design command in research preview brings Claude Design's artboard workflow directly into the CLI and Desktop. Type `/design a few options for {feature}` and Claude reads your existing codebase, matches your current UI style, and generates multiple editable artboard mockups as Artifacts — you pick a favorite, tweak it visually, then say the word and Claude implements it. Available to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers. Eliminates the context switch between design and code for the entire early-UI exploration phase.

name: mattpocock/skills — ~220K Stars; 21 Engineering Skills From Matt Pocock's Own .agents Directory
hook: Matt Pocock — the TypeScript educator behind Total TypeScript — published his personal .agents directory in March 2026. The repo has grown to ~220K stars and 21 composable skills that embed real software-engineering discipline rather than vibe-coding shortcuts. The intended flow: /grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review, with /wayfinder above for multi-session coordination. The star skill is /grill-me: Claude asks every question whose prerequisites are settled in one round, numbers each with a recommended answer, and waits for your input before touching the keyboard — 893K installs on Skillselion as of Aug 10. MIT. Works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode.

name: OthmanAdi/planning-with-files — 26.2K Stars; Manus-Style Crash-Proof Planning for Claude Code
hook: Implements the persistent file-based planning pattern credited with Manus's $2B acquisition — adapted as a drop-in Claude Code skill. Every long-running task writes a task_plan.md with phases, progress, and decisions; a per-turn re-injection hook prevents context rot between tool calls; a deterministic completion gate blocks Claude from marking work done before every phase is ticked off; session recovery works after /clear and compaction. Updated August 18 with a new PreCompact hook that fires on both /compact and autoCompact, and a /plan-goal slash command that composes with Claude Code's own /goal. Works across Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and 60+ agents. 26.2K stars.

name: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills — ~203K Stars; Day 30; 4 Rules That Stop Claude Breaking Code
hook: Day 30 in the digest — the longest-running item in the current tracking window — and still the most-starred CLAUDE.md framework in the ecosystem at ~203K stars. A CLAUDE.md encoding Andrej Karpathy's four rules: Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution. Each rule blocks a specific failure mode — unfounded assumptions, unnecessary abstraction, unintended side-effects, vague success criteria. Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 60+ other agents.

name: obra/superpowers — ~272K Stars; Day 8; Full Dev Methodology as Skills
hook: ~272,000 stars — the most-starred Claude Code skills framework on GitHub. Jesse Vincent (@obra) and Prime Radiant built a complete software-development methodology as chainable skills: brainstorm before you type, plan in bite-sized tasks, enforce TDD (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR), and pass code review before merge. 14+ skills cover the full dev lifecycle; v5.0 added native support for Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI. Accepted into the official Anthropic Claude Code plugin marketplace January 15, 2026.

name: affaan-m/ECC — ~241K Stars; Day 25; Agent OS for Claude Code
hook: ~241,000 stars. Ships 67+ specialist agents, 278+ skill definitions, 94+ command shims, and lifecycle hooks for Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and Codex across 12 language ecosystems — including code review, TDD, security scanning, documentation generation, CI/CD optimization, and a pattern-extraction system that learns from your own dev history.

name: NousResearch/hermes-agent — ~232K Stars; Day 8; Self-Improving AI Agent That Learns From Every Task
hook: ~232,000 stars, 44.9K forks. Open-source autonomous agent from NousResearch that creates skills from experience and searches past conversations — building a user model across sessions that gets smarter without manual updates. A bundled Claude Code skill delegates coding tasks directly to Claude Code CLI from the Hermes terminal; supports Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI surfaces; built-in cron scheduler; parallel subagents via isolated execution. MIT.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — ~99K Stars; Day 25; 65% Fewer Output Tokens; Near 100K Milestone
hook: ~99,000 stars — within striking distance of the 100K milestone. Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing technical accuracy; code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). The /caveman-compress companion shrinks CLAUDE.md and other memory files by ~46%, saving input tokens on every future session permanently.

name: farion1231/cc-switch — ~127K Stars; Day 9; One Desktop App for Eight AI Coding Tools
hook: ~127,000 stars. Tauri desktop app managing Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent from a single interface. 50+ provider presets, bidirectional MCP and Skills sync, cloud sync (Dropbox/iCloud/WebDAV), system-tray switching, per-session cost analytics. macOS, Windows, and Linux.

hook: ~118,000 stars. Version 2.0 ships a Design System Generator: 161 industry-specific reasoning rules across 34 product categories generate complete, tailored design systems from a brief — color palettes, font pairings, anti-patterns, and stack-matched component patterns. 84 UI styles, 192 color palettes, 74 font pairings, 22 tech stacks; works across 14 AI coding tools. Chase AI (@Chase-H-AI) named it '#1 Claude Code Design Skill' in a video covering the v2.0 upgrade.
install: npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli && uipro init --ai claude

name: Graphify-Labs/graphify — ~107K Stars; Day 26; Knowledge Graph for Any Codebase; 70x Cost Cut
hook: Turns any codebase — plus docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs — into a queryable knowledge graph using local deterministic AST parsing (tree-sitter, 158 languages). A PreToolUse hook routes every file-search through the graph; 15 MCP tools add path tracing, dead-code detection, and architecture analysis. MindStudio benchmarks show up to 70x cost reduction on 500+ file projects. ~107K stars.
install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install

name: DietrichGebert/ponytail — ~104K Stars; Day 12; Laziness Ladder Cuts Code 54–94%
hook: ~104,000 stars. A Claude Code skill enforcing a 7-rung laziness ladder before writing a single line of custom code: stdlib first, native platform features second, existing dependencies third, one-liners before functions, and so on. Benchmarked at ~54% less code (range up to 94%), ~20% cheaper, and ~27% faster on real FastAPI + React sessions. Targets code bloat while preserving security and accessibility guardrails.

name: Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything — ~80K Stars; Day 5; Codebase Knowledge Graph in 5 Parallel Agents
hook: ~80,000 stars. Installs as a native Claude Code plugin and runs 5 specialized agents in parallel — Tree-Sitter for deterministic structural parsing (imports, exports, class hierarchy) and LLM agents for semantic summaries and business logic identification. Outputs a searchable, pannable knowledge graph with diff impact analysis, architecture tours ordered by dependency, domain views, and semantic/fuzzy search across any codebase. Compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI.

name: thedotmack/claude-mem — ~91K Stars; Day 12; Persistent Context Across Sessions
hook: ~91,000 stars. Captures everything Claude does across sessions, compresses with AI, and auto-injects relevant context via lifecycle hooks — no manual context management. Three-layer progressive-disclosure architecture (search → timeline → fetch) cuts memory token overhead by ~10x vs naively injecting full history. Works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini CLI.
